newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees solid U.S. growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees solid U.S. growth, low inflation.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Friday said he foresaw more solid growth for the U.S. economy with low inflation.
Interviewed on CNN's "Moneyline" television program, Rubin also repeated his assertion that he backed a strong dollar and that the currency had been strong for some time now.
"We have had a very strong dollar for some time ... I do feel very strongly that the strong dollar has served our nation's interest and promoted economic growth and job creation," he said.

Rubin in the interview said Japan has had slow growth for most of the last five years and "the imbalance in respect to growth may be beginning to increase Japan's trade surplus with the United States, and I think it is very important both for Japan and for the world trading community, including the United States, that Japan have solid growth and macroeconomic policy that produces demand-led growth."
Rubin said he thought it was very likely a balanced budget agreement will be achieved this year. "I think it is at least possible that the deficit this year will be below last year's," he said.
